Steve is a 1.5-year-old NM Great Dane who presented for a derm exam. Clinical signs include alopecia, dermatitis, erythema, and pruritus. No fleas were seen upon exam, so FAD was R/O. Skin scrape was done to R/O mange, which was negative. Suspect atopy and referred to a dermatologist.

Reveal the term definitions (10)
NM
Neutered Male
Alopecia
Sudden hair/fur loss
Dermatitis
A general term that describes a common skin irritation
Erythema
Redness of the skin, either in a limited area or all over
Pruritus
An uncomfortable, irritating sensation that creates an urge to scratch that can involve any part of the body
FAD
Flea allergy dermatitis
R/O
Rule out
Mange
A type of skin disease caused by parasitic mites
Atopy
The genetic tendency to develop allergic diseases such as allergic rhinitis, asthma and atopic dermatitis
Dermatologist
A doctor who specializes in treating the skin

Case 3 — Gus · Cardiovascular (Module 4)

Gus, a 12-year-old M/N Shepherd mix, presented on emergency after collapsing at home with his owners. He was cyanotic and hypoxic. Cardiac auscultation revealed a murmur and tachycardia with a HR of 180 BPM. His CRT was > 4 seconds, and after taking his BP with a Sphygmomanometer, he was hypertensive. An ECG revealed an arrhythmia. The vet suspected CHF, and while getting ready for more diagnostic tests, Gus went into CPA and asystole. CPR was performed but was unsuccessful.

Reveal the term definitions (18)
MN
Male Neutered
Cyanotic
A pathologic condition that is characterized by a bluish discoloration of the skin or mucous membrane
Hypoxic
Having too little oxygen
Cardiac auscultation
Listening to the heart with a stethoscope to characterize heart sounds and murmurs
Murmur
Sound of blood flowing through the heart, due to anything from healthy heart exertion during exercise to a diseased heart valve or other abnormality
Tachycardia
An elevated heart rate
HR
Heart Rate
BPM
Beats per minute
CRT
Capillary Refill Time
BP
Blood Pressure
Sphygmomanometer
An instrument for measuring blood pressure
Hypertensive
Elevated blood pressure
ECG
Electrocardiogram: records the electrical signal from the heart to check for different heart conditions
Arrhythmia
A condition in which the heart beats with an irregular or abnormal rhythm
CHF
Congestive heart failure: a serious condition in which the heart doesn't pump blood as efficiently as it should
CPA
Cardiopulmonary arrest
Asystole
Represents the cessation of electrical and mechanical activity of the heart
CPR
An emergency lifesaving procedure performed when the heart stops beating

Case 4 — Penny · Respiratory (Module 5)

Penny, a 4-month-old intact female Golden retriever puppy, has been coughing since the owners got her from the breeder. She was initially treated with Ab and an antitussive for kennel cough but has gotten worse. She presented dyspneic today with a RR of 10 RPM. Auscultation revealed what sounded like fluid in her lungs. Radiographs confirmed pneumonia. When using a pulse oximeter, her O2 sat was 85%, and a capnograph showed she was hypercapnic. Penny was hospitalized for O2 therapy and a transtracheal wash to determine what bacteria is causing her pneumonia. Once we know the organism, she can be treated with the correct Ab.

Reveal the term definitions (14)
Ab
Antibiotic
Antitussive
Medicines that suppress coughing, also known as cough suppressants
Dyspneic
Uncomfortable abnormal breathing
RR
Respiratory Rate
RPM
Respirations per minute
Auscultation
Listening to the internal sounds of the body, usually using a stethoscope
Radiographs
An image produced on a sensitive plate or film by X-rays, gamma rays, or similar radiation, and typically used in medical examination
Pneumonia
An infection that affects one or both lungs
Pulse oximeter
An oximeter that measures the proportion of oxygenated hemoglobin in the blood in pulsating vessels
O2 sat
Oxygen saturation
Capnograph
Monitors the concentration or partial pressure of carbon dioxide in the respiratory gases
Hypercapnic
High levels of carbon dioxide in the blood
O2
Oxygen
Transtracheal
Passing through or administered by way of the trachea

Case 5 — Piper · Gastrointestinal (Module 6)

Piper, a 4-year-old spayed Female Doberman, presented upon emergency with a distended abdomen and unsuccessful emesis attempts. The owners described it as “dry-heaving,” but nothing was coming up. Upon quick abdominal palpation and auscultation of no peristalsis in the abdomen, the vet suspects a GDV. Piper is rushed to radiography which confirms the bloat and gastric torsion. After the vet's diagnosis, Piper goes to surgery. A laparotomy is performed where the gastric volvulus is corrected, the gastric contents are emptied, and a gastropexy is performed. She was lucky to have no necrotic tissue in the abdomen and will be hospitalized to monitor her for the next few days.

Reveal the term definitions (13)
Spayed
To sterilize by removing the ovaries
Emesis
The action or process of vomiting
Abdominal palpation
The examination of the abdomen for crepitus of the abdominal wall, for any abdominal tenderness, or for abdominal masses
Auscultation
Listening to the internal sounds of the body, usually using a stethoscope
Peristalsis
The involuntary constriction and relaxation of the muscles of the intestine or another canal, creating wave-like movements that push the contents of the canal forward
GDV
Gastric dilatation and volvulus
Radiography
An imaging technique using X-rays, gamma rays, or similar ionizing radiation and non-ionizing radiation to view the internal form of an object
Gastric Torsion
An abnormal rotation of the stomach twisting on its longitudinal axis
Laparotomy
A surgical procedure involving a surgical incision through the abdominal wall to gain access into the abdominal cavity
Gastric Volvulus
An abnormal rotation of the stomach on its mesenteric axis
Gastric
Of the stomach
Gastropexy
A surgical operation in which the stomach is sutured to the abdominal wall or the diaphragm
Necrotic
The death of most or all of the cells in an organ or tissue due to disease, injury, or failure of the blood supply

Case 6 — Chuck · Endocrine (Module 7)

Chuck is a 14-year-old DLH on steroid therapy for asthma who presents PU/PD, anorexic, and lethargic. Chuck has lost 4 lbs in the last 3 months. The veterinary technician draws blood from his jugular vein and performs a cystocentesis to collect a urine sample for diagnostic lab work. Chuck's BG is 450 g/dl, which is hyperglycemic. He also has increased ketones and glucosuria. The vet diagnoses him with DM, which is caused by decreased pancreatic insulin production. The owners are sent home with insulin and a glucometer to monitor Chuck at home. They are told their timing of getting him in was good, as he could have experienced DKA. Chuck is scheduled for a recheck in 1 week and a glucose curve.

Reveal the term definitions (17)
DLH
Domestic Long Hair
PU/PD
Polyuria and polydipsia
Anorexic
Loss of appetite
Lethargic
A state of weariness that involves diminished energy, mental capacity, and motivation
Lbs
Pounds
Jugular vein
Major blood vessels that stretch from the head to the upper chest
Cystocentesis
A common clinical technique used to obtain a sample of urine directly from the urinary bladder of dogs and cats when collecting a voided sample is not preferred
BG
Blood glucose
Hyperglycemic
High blood glucose (blood sugar)
Ketones
A type of chemical that the liver produces when it breaks down fats
Glucosuria
The presence of glucose in the urine
DM
Diabetes Mellitus
Pancreatic insulin
The most important hormone that the pancreas produces is insulin. Its role is to lower glucose levels in the bloodstream and promote the storage of glucose in fat, muscle, liver and other body tissues
Insulin
A hormone created by the pancreas that controls the amount of glucose in the bloodstream at any given moment
Glucometer
A small device called a glucose meter or glucometer measures how much sugar is in the blood sample
DKA
Diabetic ketoacidosis, a serious complication of diabetes that can be life-threatening
Glucose Curve
Serial measurements of blood glucose during the duration of action of insulin

Case 7 — Charlie · Nervous (Module 8)

Charlie, an 11-year-old mixed breed canine, presents with ataxia, an abnormal gait, a loss of proprioception, and seizures. This is not normal for Charlie, so the vet puts epilepsy low on the DDX list. It is suspected to be a problem with the CNS, and a CSF tap and analysis is recommended, along with an MRI done under anesthesia. The R/O list includes vestibular disease, meningitis, encephalitis, encephalomyelitis, or another encephalopathy.

Reveal the term definitions (16)
Ataxia
Impaired balance or coordination, can be due to damage to brain, nerves, or muscles
Gait
Pattern of movement of the limbs of animals
Proprioception
The sense that lets us perceive the location, movement, and action of parts of the body
Seizures
A sudden, uncontrolled burst of electrical activity in the brain
Epilepsy
A disorder in which nerve cell activity in the brain is disturbed, causing seizures
DDX
Differential Diagnosis
CNS
Central Nervous System
CSF tap and analysis
A medical procedure in which a needle is inserted into the spinal canal to collect cerebrospinal fluid for diagnostic testing. The main reason for a CSF tap is to help diagnose diseases of the central nervous system, including the brain and spine
MRI
Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) is a non-invasive imaging technology that produces three-dimensional detailed anatomical images
Anesthesia
The use of medicines to prevent pain during surgery and other procedures
R/O
Rule Out
Vestibular disease
A sudden, non-progressive disturbance of balance
Meningitis
An inflammation (swelling) of the protective membranes covering the brain and spinal cord
Encephalitis
Inflammation of the brain
Encephalomyelitis
Inflammation of the brain and spinal cord
Encephalopathy
Any disease of the brain that alters brain function or structure

Review items

Twenty-four items across four sections follow. Answer each one to complete the review.

quiz.q: Which abbreviation means as needed?
quiz.exp: PRN = as needed. NPO = nothing by mouth; PO = by mouth; QID = four times a day.

quiz.q: Which abbreviation means nothing by mouth?
quiz.exp: NPO = nothing by mouth — often ordered before anesthesia or surgery.

quiz.q: OD refers to which eye?
quiz.exp: OD = right eye, OS = left eye, OU = both eyes.

quiz.q: In Gastr/o, what does adding the /o create?
quiz.exp: Gastr is the word root; adding the combining vowel o makes Gastr/o a combining form, which lets the root join a suffix that begins with a consonant.

quiz.q: Epi- and Hyper- are examples of…
quiz.exp: Both attach to the front of a term. Epi- = above/upon; Hyper- = excessive.

quiz.q: The suffix -logy means…
quiz.exp: Contrast -pathy (disease), -oma (tumor), and -osis (abnormal condition).

quiz.q: PU/PD describes…
quiz.exp: Polyuria / polydipsia — a classic endocrine presentation, seen in Chuck's diabetes mellitus case.

quiz.q: A patient in dorsal recumbency is positioned…
opts: With the sternum on the table
quiz.exp: Dorsal recumbency: positioned on their back.

quiz.q: A patient in sternal (ventral) recumbency is positioned so that…
opts: The sternum lies in contact with the table
They lie on their left side
They stand squarely on all four limbs
quiz.exp: Sternal/ventral recumbency: positioned in a way that the patient's sternum lies in contact with the table.

quiz.q: “The elbow is proximal to the carpus” means the elbow is…
opts: Closer to the point of attachment to the body
Further from the point of attachment to the body
quiz.exp: Proximal = nearer the trunk or point of attachment; distal = further away.

quiz.q: Which term means pertaining to above the skin?
quiz.exp: Epi- (above) + derm (skin) + -al. Subcutaneous is pertaining to under the skin.

quiz.q: The root hepat refers to which organ?
quiz.exp: Hepat = liver. It also appears in the H of the DHLPP vaccine — hepatitis.

quiz.q: Riley's chart records bilat lameness and muscle atrophy. Atrophy means…
opts: Body tissue or an organ wasting away
quiz.exp: Atrophy is tissue or an organ wasting away, especially as a result of the degeneration of cells.

quiz.q: R/O in a medical record stands for…
quiz.exp: R/O = rule out. It appears in Riley's, Steve's, and Charlie's cases.

quiz.q: Steve's exam records alopecia and pruritus. Pruritus is…
opts: An irritating sensation that creates an urge to scratch
quiz.exp: Alopecia is the hair loss; erythema is the redness; an ulcer is the eroded area.

quiz.q: FAD stands for…
quiz.exp: Flea Allergy Dermatitis — the most common dermatological condition diagnosed in dogs in the US.

quiz.q: Gus presented cyanotic with a CRT greater than 4 seconds. CRT is…
quiz.exp: Capillary refill time. A prolonged CRT indicates poor perfusion.

quiz.q: Piper's suspected GDV stands for…
quiz.exp: Gastric = of the stomach, dilatation = abnormal stretching, volvulus = twisting on itself.

quiz.q: Chuck's bloodwork shows glucosuria and a BG of 450, consistent with…
quiz.exp: Diabetes mellitus, caused by decreased pancreatic insulin production.

quiz.q: Give 1 tab PO TID ac translated for the owner's label reads…
opts: 1 tablet by mouth twice a day, after meals
1 tablet by mouth three times a day, after meals
1 tablet in the ear three times a day
1 tablet by mouth three times a day, before meals
quiz.exp: PO = by mouth, TID = three times a day, ac = before meals.

quiz.q: “Give one tablet twice a day as needed for pain” written in record abbreviations is…
opts: 1 tab PO BID prn for pain
1 tab PO TID prn for pain
1 tab SQ BID prn for pain
1 tab PO QID ac for pain
quiz.exp: BID = twice a day; prn = as needed; PO = by mouth.

quiz.q: Administer 2 gtts OS QID means…
opts: 2 tablets by mouth four times a day
2 drops in the left eye four times a day
2 drops in the right eye four times a day
2 drops in both eyes twice a day
quiz.exp: gtts = drops, OS = left eye, QID = four times a day.

quiz.q: Which of these is a parenteral route?
quiz.exp: Parenteral routes do not include the GI tract. The other three all deliver medication through the GI tract, making them enteral.

quiz.q: FVRCP protects cats against Feline Viral Rhinotracheitis, Calicivirus and…
quiz.exp: FVR = Feline Viral Rhinotracheitis, C = Calicivirus, P = Panleukopenia. FeLV is a separate vaccine.
